correctness.rationale: Strict convexity confines diameter pairs to vertices. A diameter endpoint has strictly positive axial projection on each tangent ray, ensuring compact facet cap sections. Each cap area equals a positive constant times t^(d-1) exactly; independence and beta convolution produce ((d-1)!)^2/(2d-2)!, and the quadratic chord Taylor remainder yields O(epsilon^(2d-1)) by uniform cone transversality. Summing disjoint ordered diameter pairs proves the full theorem. Independent exact benchmark computations and sampled Euclidean geometry checks succeeded; simulations are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A universal d>=3 geometric probability law for arbitrary convex polytopes: sharp exponent 2d-2 and an explicit nonzero coefficient computable from all diametral facet cones, with exact all-dimensional regular simplex/cube constants. This supplies an important tail input for extreme-distance calculations and distinguishes facet-area sampling from interior and random-line models; its value does not rely on claiming a sample-maximum theorem.
